title: Environmental Design
hook: Your desk is either helping you work or quietly pulling you toward your phone. There's no neutral.
statement: Your environment is stronger than your discipline.
explainer: You're in your space for hours every day. If it's full of cues for the wrong stuff, you're fighting it all day. Set it up right and it pulls you along.
sop: Walk through your workspace and note every visible cue.
Score your Environment 1 to 10 for the behavior you want.
Hide or remove every trigger for the behavior you don't want.
Add one visible cue for the behavior you do want.
Re-check monthly, because spaces slowly drift back.
equation_example: Environment 8, Exposure Time 6 hours a day. 8 × 6 = 48. Higher means your space is nudging you the right way hour after hour. Lower means you're using willpower to fight a room that's working against you.
question: Pick the one space that's fighting you and change one thing in it today.
closing_statement: Discipline fades. A well-built environment doesn't.
caption:
Principle Nº 135: Environmental Design

Your environment is stronger than your discipline.
